records.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR telemetry name maps to the 2004 Lamborghini Murciélago R-GT race specification, not to the road-going Murciélago E-gear. The exact 2004 R-GT chassis documented by RM Sotheby's used a Holinger six-speed sequential gearbox; the R-GT program was developed by Reiter Engineering with Audi Sport and ran in FIA GT/Le Mans-type competition. The local PMR observation is implementation evidence only: it is pinned to Steam content build 24725083, and its D-shaped rim, integrated display, shift lights, closed rim, and pedal/shift-technique values are not transferred into the authentic baseline unless independently established.

records.specification_basis: The exact 2004 chassis source and Lamborghini-attributed specification both identify a six-speed gearbox, and the PMR observation independently reports six forward gears. Both real-car sources identify the target 2004 R-GT gearbox as sequential. The exact chassis 1057 cockpit gallery shows a sequential gear lever, supporting sequential-stick actuation. This is medium confidence because the photographic source does not provide a technical control specification or a complete shift-procedure description. The documented exact 2004 R-GT gearbox is sequential, so its shift pattern is sequential rather than a standard H gate.
